title: Capgras Syndrome: You Are Not Who You Think You Are
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss Capgras syndrome (cap gras, Capgras delusion), a delusional misidentification disorder in which the sufferer believes close family members or others have been replaced by identical impostors. They cover its prevalence estimates, its link to Alzheimer's, schizophrenia and other psychotic disorders, and contrast it with prosopagnosia (face blindness) and skin conductance findings. They describe Freudian and psychodynamic explanations, the organic/brain-based theories, and the Ramachandran and Hirstein memory-file explanation. Case examples include DS, a man who came to believe he himself was an impostor, and violent incidents. Related conditions discussed are Fregoli syndrome, Cotard syndrome, intermetamorphosis, and reduplicative paramnesia. The episode closes with a listener email about Mormon sealing and multiple spouses, and the outro.

segments.title: Opening banter and introduction to Capgras
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the episode on Capgras syndrome, a delusion in which people close to the sufferer are believed to be replaced by impostors, and note its difficulty for both sufferer and misidentified person.

segments.title: Prevalence and association with Alzheimer's
segments.summary: Discussion of estimated prevalence among psychiatric patients and Alzheimer's patients, and the description of a patient who believed she had many identical husbands.

segments.title: Prosopagnosia contrast and emotional recognition
segments.summary: Comparison of Capgras with prosopagnosia; skin conductance studies show face recognition with emotional response in prosopagnosia but lack of emotional response in Capgras, with recognition intact.

segments.title: Causes: Freudian theory and organic brain explanations
segments.summary: The early psychodynamic and Freudian explanation is dismissed; researchers now favor organic brain causes, with comorbidity to epilepsy, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and Alzheimer's, and a combined mental and physical explanation.

segments.title: Ramachandran and Hirstein memory theory and case of DS
segments.summary: Ramachandran and Hirstein propose a memory-management problem where patients create new files for familiar people; the case of DS, who believed his father and himself were impostors, and violent incidents are described. Treatment is limited.

segments.title: Related disorders: Fregoli, Cotard, intermetamorphosis
segments.summary: Overview of related delusional syndromes: Fregoli syndrome (people are disguised loved ones), Cotard syndrome (belief one is dead or missing body parts), and intermetamorphosis (people close to you switch identities).

segments.title: Closing remarks and search tips
segments.summary: Hosts close the discussion on brain research, mention the documentary The Impostor, and suggest searching the topic on HowStuffWorks.

segments.title: Listener email on Mormon sealing
segments.summary: A former member writes that men can be sealed to multiple women in the LDS church even though plural marriage is no longer practiced, and asks for a podcast on the church.
